text:
angela: Quick sync – we discovered a bunch of org-level API keys that were created outside project flows (projectless keys). They show up in billing as org traffic but our routing/quotas assume project attribution. Thoughts on how to handle routing + telemetry for these?

rajesh: Ugh. Yep. We currently map quota by project id in the token claim. If token lacks project claim we fallback to org default bucket which is pretty coarse.

angela: Right. Two quick options I sketched: 1) Block projectless keys from issuing (UX change) 2) Keep allowing, but create an inferred-project rule in routing that pins first encountered project for attribution and emits 'inferred_project' telemetry tag.

taylor: Inferred project could be surprising. What if a key is legitimately used across multiple projects/teams? Attribution would muddy usage. :thinking_face:

angela: Good point. We could only infer for keys that have consistent origin header for N days, otherwise keep org bucket and emit a sample telemetry event for manual review.

rajesh: We also need to consider console UI. If we expose "projectless" keys in the key management page, teams will expect a way to bind them later. Maybe add a lightweight "assign to project" action and a warning about quota routing.

liz: From quota enforcement side, we can't do both per-request dynamic reassignment and strict SLOs. If we allow pinning at first-use, we must accept sticky routing (affinity). That affects autoscaling and capacity planning.

angela: Agreed. Proposal: keep issuance allowed, default to org bucket, surface a banner in console: "This key is projectless — click to assign for per-project quotas." Add telemetry events: key.created, key.assigned, key.inferred_assignment, key.conflict. For routing, only honor inferred_assignment after 48h of consistent same-project usage and log conflicts.

infra-bot: deploy-notify: canary rollout of key-listing UX change started to eng-frontend at 2024-08-01T14:32Z (build 2024.8.1-canary).

taylor: Implementation detail: token structure currently looks like: 
```
{
  "iss": "redwood",
  "sub": "key:org_ABC",
  "claims": { "org": "org_ABC", "project": "proj_123" }
}
```
So projectless keys simply have no project claim. We can add an internal header `X-Redwood-Inferred-Project: proj_123` at the routing layer for debugging + telemetry, but we must NOT rely on it for billing until it's promoted.

rajesh: Also add an oplog event for any inferred assignment so compliance/audit can reconstruct. Maybe `audit.inferred_project` with user + sample requests.

liz: For quotas: add a short-circuit rule: if key.assigned -> use project bucket; else if key.inferred && inference_age >= 48h && no conflicts -> use inferred project bucket; else -> use org bucket. That keeps SLOs inviolable.

angela: Sounds good. UX copy for the console banner draft: "This API key isn't linked to a project. Link it to get per-project quotas and clearer billing. You can also let Redwood suggest a project after steady usage is detected (needs ~48h)."

taylor: One more internal API note: telemetry events should include `sample_rate` on inferred events so we can ramp up/down collection. Start small (1%) and increase if we need to debug.

angela: Action items: 1) Rajesh + Taylor add routing rule and header at edge (PR for edge-proxy) 2) Liz wire quota decision logic (feature flag) 3) UX: add banner + "assign" action (canary) 4) Telemetry: events + sampling (start 1%). I'll file the RFC and link.

rajesh: I'll do the edge PR and add unit tests for conflict cases.

taylor: I'll add the debug header and a small toggle in env for the 48h grace.

liz: I'll prototype quota rule behind flag and run load sim.

angela: Thanks all — ping me in thread when PRs landed so we can coordinate canary. :thumbsup:
